title: MV Force game.exe to use dedicated GPU

posts.author: Krosis
posts.body:
Hey! In my project (mv) I've added several plugins that increased the graphic demand of the game. The problem is that even though that happened, Windows 11 (laptop) still considers it low-demand program and runs it on iGPU and it never utilizes my RTX3070.
So I basically have a 40-80 fps game instead of 144 fps and it sometimes even crashes. Yes I can easily fix that by manualy changing the settings from the Control Panel and force it to run on dedicated GPU, but what about the players? Some of them may encounter the same problem but not everyone can fix it by themselves.
1. So, is there a way to modify the .exe file of a deployed project in order to force it to run through the GPU instead of iGPU?
2. Or a trick which will make the OS see it as heavier program and auto choose the GPU?
2. Will that affect Canvas mode somehow or that is not something I should be concerned about?

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
I don't know if this'll make Windows detect it properly, but if you use the Community_Basic plugin, I'd set rendering mode to WebGL in its plugin parameters.
If that doesn't work, then I have no idea.

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
Standalone RMMV games run in a NWJS app, which is essentially a small Chromium-based browser.
NWJS might support a command-line argument that affects which GPU is used to run the application? If so, you could add that to the
chromium-args
section of your game's manifest file (
package.json
). I just had a quick look here, though, and didn't see anything promising:
Command Line Options - NW.js Documentation
docs.nwjs.io
A quick search online suggests that Electron (an alternative to NW) has a
--force_high_performance_gpu
arg. I don't know whether that's from an updated version of Chromium, or something specific to Electron. Either way I tried that, as well as
--in_process_gpu
(to hit your 2nd point), but neither one seemed to change which GPU was used in playtest.
Canvas/WebGL render mode is initialised via the core scripts, after the app has launched. The game tries to do some WebGL stuff, and if that fails, it uses Canvas (cf
Graphics.hasWebGL
in rpg_core.js).

posts.author: bass2yang
posts.body:
To add to caethyril, here's a few other chromium args you can try:
Code:
"chromium-args" : "--in-process-gpu ignore-gpu-blocklist --force-gpu-mem-available-mb=14000 --force-gpu-rasterization --enable-native-gpu-memory-buffers --enable-gpu-memory-buffer-compositor-resources",

The whole problem comes from the fact that win11 considers RPG Maker games as "light" programs and It runs them on the weaker iGPU.
